summary.business_type: Pre-launch programmatic directory site (airline office locations worldwide) — Astro frontend + headless WordPress CMS
top_findings: robots.txt (Disallow: /) and site-wide noindex meta correctly block all crawlers today via an intentional STAGING flag — but this is a launch-blocker checklist item, and it must not be lifted before the items below are fixed

All 6 published location pages contain literal Lorem Ipsum placeholder body copy and a fake phone number (+1-XXX-XXX-XXXX) wired to a dead href="#" link instead of a tel: link — 100% of the site's core content product is placeholder data
A live FAQPage JSON-LD block on the Algiers office page contains fabricated Q&A ("question 1"/"answer 1") — fake structured data is a policed spam pattern independent of the thin-content issue

/home is a leaked default WordPress page duplicating the real homepage (/), with its own schema self-identifying AS the homepage URL — will create a duplicate-content collision the moment STAGING flips off

Structured data (Yoast JSON-LD) references image URLs on airlineslocations.com/wp-content/... that 404 — media actually lives on cms.airlineslocations.com; breaks rich-result image eligibility sitewide

SXO analysis of real competitor SERPs shows the page template is missing every structural element (address, hours, map, FAQ, LocalBusiness schema) that Google's own AI-synthesized answers pull from competing directory sites for these exact query types

The WordPress default "Hello world!" post is live on the homepage's "Latest Blog Posts" section, publicly attributed to a real personal Gmail address (gradyrpollock@gmail.com) — a privacy exposure, not just a polish issue

Headless-Chrome (Lighthouse/PSI) requests get HTTP 403 from Hostinger's edge WAF while plain HTTP fetches succeed — risk that Google's own PageSpeed/Search Console tooling could be blocked the same way post-launch
quick_wins: Add "home" to RESERVED_SLUGS in src/lib/wp.ts (or delete the WP "Home" page) to kill the /home duplicate before launch
Change the "Call Now" href from "#" to a tel: link (even with placeholder digits) so the CTA mechanism is testable pre-launch
Fix the JSON-LD image domain bug so ImageObject/thumbnailUrl point at cms.airlineslocations.com instead of the 404ing frontend domain
Remove/replace the fake FAQPage "question 1"/"answer 1" placeholder schema on the Algiers page
Delete the default WordPress "Hello world!" post and scrub the personal Gmail byline/sameAs CMS-origin disclosure
Set a real Cache-Control (not no-store) on the statically prerendered homepage so Hostinger's edge CDN can actually cache it
301-normalize trailing-slash and case-variant URLs to the single lowercase canonical form instead of self-canonicalizing to whatever was requested
Add /airlines and /blog to the sitemap's STATIC_PATHS list

categories.name: Technical SEO
what_works: Full security header set present and consistent (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, CSP upgrade-insecure-requests, Permissions-Policy)
HTTPS + HSTS enforced sitewide; www correctly resolves to apex with no redirect loop
Server-side rendering confirmed non-JS-dependent for crawling (is_spa: false) — no CSR barrier
404s return real HTTP 404, not soft-404
Sitemap.xml is valid, well-formed XML, well under size limits, no broken URLs
URL hierarchy correctly mirrors WordPress's parent/child page tree per the project's design
The STAGING gate architecture (robots.txt, noindex meta, Cache-Control) is centralized behind one env var, which is good engineering even though 3 real bugs were found underneath it
No redirect chains on any of the 10 sitemap URLs

findings.title: robots.txt (Disallow: /) blocks all crawling — intentional but must not ship this way
findings.description: robots.txt returns 'User-agent: *\nDisallow: /' and every page also carries a noindex,nofollow meta tag, both driven by the STAGING env var (defaults true). This is correct pre-launch behavior, not a bug, but the code comments confirm the prerendered homepage/404 bake the noindex tag in at build time — an env-only flip at launch will not clear it from those two routes without a rebuild.
findings.recommendation: At launch: set STAGING=false in Hostinger's env panel AND rebuild. Verify post-launch that robots.txt serves Allow: / plus a Sitemap: line, and that a fresh curl of / specifically (not just an SSR page) has no noindex tag.

findings.title: /home is a near-duplicate, thin-content page competing with the real homepage
findings.description: /home is a separate live WordPress page (likely WP's leftover default install page) with an empty content body, its own self-referencing canonical, and a generic Yoast-default title — distinct from the real homepage. Root cause: RESERVED_SLUGS in src/lib/wp.ts excludes '', api, airlines, blog but not 'home'.
findings.recommendation: Delete the WP 'Home' page, or add 'home' to RESERVED_SLUGS so it's excluded from the page tree/routing/sitemap the same way airlines/blog already are.

findings.title: Structured data references an image domain that 404s
findings.description: The Yoast JSON-LD @graph's ImageObject/thumbnailUrl point to https://airlineslocations.com/wp-content/uploads/... which does not exist on the Astro frontend domain (confirmed 404). The real media lives at cms.airlineslocations.com, which is what og:image/twitter:image correctly use on the same page.
findings.recommendation: Either strip Yoast's raw @graph and have Astro emit its own correctly-domained schema, or rewrite cms.airlineslocations.com media URLs inside the passed-through JSON-LD the same way OG image URLs are already handled.

findings.title: Duplicate URL variants: trailing slash and case are not normalized
findings.description: Both a trailing-slash and a mixed-case variant of the same content URL return 200 and self-canonicalize to whatever variant was requested, rather than to one canonical lowercase form — creating unlimited duplicate-content URL variants per page.
findings.recommendation: 301-redirect any trailing-slash or non-canonical-case request to the single lowercase, no-trailing-slash form at the routing layer, before the canonical tag is computed.

findings.title: og:image / twitter:image served over insecure http://
findings.description: Social preview image meta tags use http:// even though the file is reachable over HTTPS, inconsistent with the site's HSTS/CSP upgrade-insecure-requests posture elsewhere.
findings.recommendation: Force https:// when resolving the Yoast og_image URL, or set WP's siteurl to HTTPS so it's correct at the source.

findings.title: Double-encoded HTML entities in meta descriptions
findings.description: og:description/twitter:description render literal '“' and '…' character codes instead of curly quotes/ellipsis — WP's original entities have been re-escaped a second time.
findings.recommendation: Ensure Yoast description/title strings are decoded exactly once when interpolated into meta content attributes; audit for a double htmlEscape() call.

findings.title: Sitemap missing lastmod; missing /airlines and /blog
findings.description: No <lastmod> on any sitemap entry (WP REST fetch only requests 'date', not 'modified'). /airlines and /blog are live, nav-linked, hand-built pages absent from STATIC_PATHS in sitemap.xml.ts.
findings.recommendation: Add 'modified' to the WP REST _fields fetch and emit real <lastmod> values; add /airlines and /blog to STATIC_PATHS.

findings.title: Cache-Control: no-store on the statically prerendered homepage
findings.description: The homepage is prerendered static HTML at build time but is served with no-store, and Hostinger's edge (hcdn) never caches it (x-hcdn-cache-status: DYNAMIC) — every visit round-trips to origin unnecessarily. This is a deliberate STAGING-flip safety choice today.
findings.recommendation: Post-launch, once the STAGING-flip risk window has closed, move the prerendered homepage/404 to a cacheable Cache-Control (e.g. short max-age + stale-while-revalidate), leaving genuinely dynamic SSR routes on no-store.

findings.title: Hero background image not preload-hinted (likely LCP element)
findings.description: The homepage hero uses a CSS background-image, which the browser can't start fetching until CSS is parsed — a common LCP-delay pattern, unlike the header logo which correctly uses fetchpriority="high".
findings.recommendation: Add for the hero image, or convert it to an with fetchpriority="high".

findings.title: Hotlinked third-party image with no explicit dimensions (CLS risk)
findings.description: The homepage 'About Us' section hotlinks an Unsplash image with no width/height attributes, unlike every other image on the page.
findings.recommendation: Set explicit width/height (or aspect-ratio), and consider self-hosting instead of hotlinking a third party.

findings.title: Placeholder dead links (href="#") and fake phone number in production markup
findings.description: Homepage hero 'Call Now' and 'Learn About Us' CTAs both point to href="#".
findings.recommendation: Wire up real destinations before launch — a tel: link for the phone CTA, a real About page for the second.

findings.title: Missing og:image/twitter:image on non-WP static pages
findings.description: Homepage, /airlines, /blog, and the airline hub pages have no og:image/twitter:image at all, unlike WP office detail pages.
findings.recommendation: Add a default/fallback OG image (site logo or branded card) in BaseLayout.astro for pages without a WP-sourced image.

findings.title: WebSite JSON-LD lacks SearchAction; no Organization schema site-wide
findings.description: The homepage's only JSON-LD block is a minimal WebSite type with no potentialAction/SearchAction despite a working site search form, and no Organization entity exists anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Add SearchAction once content is real — improves eligibility for sitelinks search box signals.

categories.name: Content Quality
what_works: Structural hierarchy (H1/H2/H3, breadcrumbs, JSON-LD WebPage/BreadcrumbList) is present and reasonably clean
datePublished/dateModified are correctly wired into schema — a real foundation for freshness signals once content is real
The site is honest about its non-official status (clear 'no official affiliation with any airline' disclaimer)

findings.title: Lorem Ipsum placeholder content confirmed on all 6 published location pages
findings.description: Every location page (2 Qatar Airways, 4 Turkish Airlines) renders the identical Lorem Ipsum body copy and identical placeholder phone string +1-XXX-XXX-XXXX on a dead href="#" link. No page has an address, hours, or map. This is the CMS/template default filler, confirming the per-office data-entry step has not happened for any published location. Weighted E-E-A-T score: ~2/100 (Trustworthiness, the highest-weighted factor, scores ~3/100 due to fabricated contact data).
findings.recommendation: Do not lift the noindex/robots.txt gate until every published location page has real, verified contact data. Audit the CMS content-entry workflow so pages can't publish without required phone/address/hours fields.

findings.title: Fabricated FAQPage schema ("question 1"/"answer 1") live in production
findings.description: The Algiers office page publishes an FAQPage JSON-LD block with literal placeholder Q&A text, rendered both visibly and in structured data. Google's guidelines explicitly prohibit structured data that doesn't reflect real content; fabricated FAQ markup is an actively policed spam pattern.
findings.recommendation: Either populate real FAQ content or strip the FAQPage schema and visible FAQ block entirely before any page goes live.

findings.title: WordPress default 'Hello world!' post live and visible on the homepage, exposing a personal email
findings.description: The unedited WP scaffold post is surfaced in a styled 'Latest Blog Posts' section on the homepage itself, attributed to a raw personal Gmail address (gradyrpollock@gmail.com) as the public byline, and its author schema's sameAs field discloses the headless CMS origin URL.
findings.recommendation: Delete or replace the post, remove it from the homepage blog section, and scrub the personal email/CMS-origin disclosure from public author schema.

findings.title: Programmatic/scaled-content risk under Google's site reputation abuse policy
findings.description: 6 near-identical template pages where the only unique element is the city name and the 'unique' body is the same Lorem Ipsum copy-pasted across all of them is close to a textbook example of what Google's scaled content abuse policy targets. If replicated across hundreds/thousands of location pages without real per-location data, the site risks a site-wide demotion once indexed.
findings.recommendation: Fix the content pipeline (not just these 6 pages) before scaling page volume — require real, verified data per page before publish.

findings.title: 5 of 6 location pages have no real, location-specific image
findings.description: The homepage 'Latest Pages' grid and location pages themselves render a generic placeholder icon for 5 of 6 offices; the 6th reuses one unrelated generic stock photo as both hero and thumbnail.
findings.recommendation: Add real, location-specific images for all published location pages before launch.

categories.name: On-Page SEO
what_works: Title tags on location pages are well-formed and intent-matching (e.g. 'Qatar Airways Paris Office in France - airlineslocations.com')
H1s match page intent and title tags
Breadcrumb navigation exists and is visible on-page

findings.title: Meta description is null on location pages
findings.description: The representative location page (Qatar Airways Paris) has no meta description at all, where every reviewed ranking competitor for this query type has a filled, keyword-rich meta description.
findings.recommendation: Populate real, location-specific meta descriptions once real content exists; do not auto-generate from Lorem Ipsum excerpts.

findings.title: Body headings (H2/H3) are non-semantic Lorem Ipsum artifacts
findings.description: Section headings on location pages literally read 'The standard Lorem Ipsum passage, used since 1966' and 'Section 1.10.32 of de Finibus Bonorum et Malorum' — self-identifying as placeholder text to any visitor or crawler.
findings.recommendation: Replace with real, location-specific section headings (Contact Information, Airport Details, Services, Map, Head Office, FAQs) once real content lands.

findings.title: Weak/irrelevant internal linking on location pages
findings.description: The related-page sidebar on the Paris office page surfaces exactly one link — 'Qatar Airways Algiers Office in Algeria' — which is geographically irrelevant to a Paris searcher.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a real 'nearby/related offices' module surfacing same-airline or same-region pages.

findings.title: Hardcoded, unlocalized disclaimer text
findings.description: The footer disclaimer references 'the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN)' on a France office page — a hardcoded string not localized per country, stemming from a missing dynamic field rather than a copy-quality issue.
findings.recommendation: Make the disclaimer's regulatory-body reference a dynamic field per country, or use a generic non-country-specific disclaimer.

findings.title: No HQ/head-office pointer section on location pages
findings.description: Competitors commonly pair local-office info with a short 'Head Office' block for searchers who land on the wrong page tier; the target template has no such section.
findings.recommendation: Add a short head-office pointer block (address + contact) once real data exists.

categories.name: Schema & Structured Data
what_works: 100% JSON-LD format (no deprecated Microdata/RDFa)
@context, @type validity, and ISO 8601 dates all pass validation
WebPage/BreadcrumbList/WebSite present consistently across all content pages
SSR delivery means structured data is crawlable without JS execution

findings.title: Fabricated FAQPage content live in production JSON-LD
findings.description: The Algiers page's FAQPage block contains literal 'question 1'/'answer 1' placeholder Q&A pairs in structured data, not just visible copy.
findings.recommendation: Populate real FAQ content or remove the FAQPage block before launch, independent of FAQPage's retired SERP rich-result status.

findings.title: /home vs / — conflicting self-referencing schema @id
findings.description: The /home page's WebPage node declares its own @id/url as https://airlineslocations.com/ (the real homepage's URL) while its canonical tag correctly says /home — a direct self-reference conflict layered on top of the duplicate-content issue.
findings.recommendation: Resolve together with the /home duplicate-page fix (delete the page, or make its schema self-consistent with its own canonical URL).

findings.title: No LocalBusiness/Organization entity schema anywhere
findings.description: No page carries LocalBusiness, TravelAgency, Organization, PostalAddress, GeoCoordinates, or ContactPoint schema — only wrapper types (WebPage/WebSite/BreadcrumbList) exist. This is the single highest-value schema gap for a location directory.
findings.recommendation: Wire up TravelAgency schema per office page (with parentOrganization linking to an Organization node per airline hub page) once real NAP data lands — do not generate from placeholder data; gate rendering on non-empty required fields.

findings.title: Duplicate, conflicting BreadcrumbList emitted twice per page
findings.description: Every content page except / emits two separate BreadcrumbList graphs with different root labels and trailing-slash conventions — one from the WordPress-sourced @graph, one from the Astro Breadcrumbs.astro component.
findings.recommendation: Emit only one — recommend keeping the Astro-generated version (matches the visible on-page breadcrumb) and suppressing the WordPress-sourced duplicate.

findings.title: WebPage/BreadcrumbList @id trailing-slash mismatch vs. canonical URL
findings.description: The WordPress-sourced graph's self-referencing @id/url carries a trailing slash that doesn't match the actual served canonical URL (no trailing slash).
findings.recommendation: Normalize so the schema @id matches the canonical URL exactly.

findings.title: Homepage's WebSite schema is a bare 118-byte stub
findings.description: The homepage is the one page still emitting only a minimal WebSite block with no @id or SearchAction, inconsistent with every other page's richer graph.
findings.recommendation: Bring / in line with other pages: add @id and a SearchAction pointing at the working site search.

categories.name: Performance
what_works: TTFB for both static and dynamic pages falls within 'good' territory (0.4–0.7s) even without edge caching
Architecture is sound: hybrid rendering correctly separates prerendered static routes from live SSR content routes

findings.title: Homepage is served with Cache-Control: no-store despite being fully static
findings.description: The prerendered homepage is never cached at Hostinger's edge (x-hcdn-cache-status: DYNAMIC) — every visit round-trips to origin. This is architecturally unnecessary for a build-time-static page and is the highest-impact, lowest-effort performance fix identified.
findings.recommendation: Set a real Cache-Control (e.g. public, max-age=0, s-maxage=300, stale-while-revalidate=60) on the prerendered homepage/404 responses; leave genuinely dynamic SSR routes on no-store or a short s-maxage.

findings.title: Real lab Core Web Vitals (LCP/INP/CLS) could not be measured — headless Chrome gets HTTP 403 from the hosting edge
findings.description: Both local Lighthouse and Google PSI failed to render the site; plain HTTP fetches succeeded, isolating the block to Hostinger's hcdn edge WAF fingerprinting real headless-browser navigation, independent of the STAGING gate. If not specific to this audit environment, Google's own PageSpeed Insights and Search Console page-experience tooling could hit the same 403 post-launch.
findings.recommendation: Test PSI against a public build before launch; if it also 403s, have Hostinger allowlist Google's Lighthouse/PSI fetcher and Googlebot at the hcdn WAF layer.

findings.title: WP-backed pages run ~150-200ms slower TTFB than the static homepage
findings.description: Consistent with the extra per-request WordPress REST API round-trip even through the in-memory cache — this gap eats directly into the LCP budget for content pages and will widen under real load.
findings.recommendation: Investigate extending the WP REST in-memory cache TTL, or adding a short s-maxage edge-cache layer with stale-while-revalidate for content pages.

categories.name: Images
what_works: Images that do load scale correctly across all tested viewports with no distortion
Most images carry explicit width/height attributes (the one hotlinked exception is flagged separately)

findings.title: 5 of 6 location pages show a broken/placeholder image icon instead of real photography
findings.description: The homepage 'Latest Pages' grid and the Qatar Airways hub page both visibly render generic gray placeholder icons for Paris, Miami, Leipzig, Nouakchott, and Nuremberg office cards — clearly readable to any visitor as 'no image uploaded yet'.
findings.recommendation: Upload real, location-specific images for all published location pages before launch.

findings.title: No location-specific imagery exists in the page template at all
findings.description: The only two tags on a location detail page are the site logo, re-served at different sizes in the header and footer — there is no city/office photo or map-image component in the template.
findings.recommendation: Add a location-relevant image/photo slot to the location-page template, matching the hero-photo or gallery pattern used by ranking competitors.

findings.title: Hotlinked third-party image with no explicit dimensions
findings.description: The homepage 'About Us' section hotlinks an Unsplash image with no width/height attributes, a CLS risk once it loads.
findings.recommendation: Set explicit dimensions and consider self-hosting instead of hotlinking a third party.

categories.name: AI Search Readiness (GEO)
what_works: Server-side rendering means no CSR/JS barrier for any AI crawler once access is opened — raw and rendered HTML are effectively identical
datePublished/dateModified are correctly wired into schema, a real foundation for freshness signals
The site-ready (non-staging) code path already produces a clean Allow: / plus sitemap reference with no bugs to fix later

findings.title: robots.txt blocks every AI crawler indiscriminately (cross-cutting with Technical SEO Critical #1)
findings.description: The blanket Disallow: / with no per-bot rules blocks GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, and Bingbot equally. Intentional pre-launch gate; tracked here as it relates specifically to AI-answer-engine visibility once lifted.
findings.recommendation: Do not lift this gate until content is real (see Content Quality Critical #1) — sequence 'flip STAGING=false' strictly after content is fixed, not before.

findings.title: No citable facts exist anywhere in location-page content
findings.description: Body content is raw Lorem Ipsum piped straight from WordPress with no fallback or validation preventing a placeholder page from publishing. No address, hours, or map exists in any form — plain text, meta, or structured. Nothing an AI answer engine could cite.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-sentence direct-answer opening ('The [Airline] office in [City] is located at [address]...') once real per-office data exists.

findings.title: Phone number is a sitewide constant, not per-office data
findings.description: The 'Call Now' number is sourced from a single supportPhone constant in src/lib/config.ts and rendered identically on every child page — even once real address/hours are added per page, the phone number will still read as one generic (and currently fake) line unless changed to per-office data.
findings.recommendation: Move phone number to a per-office CMS field; make the Call Now href a real tel: link.

findings.title: Template has no labeled NAP (Name/Address/Phone/Hours) block
findings.description: Even once real content is entered as free-form WordPress prose, it won't be reliably extractable by AI answer engines — no dl/dt/dd or schema-marked fields separate 'answer' from narrative, and no passage-length discipline exists.
findings.recommendation: Add a dedicated, semantically labeled NAP block to the location-page layout, separate from the free-form prose content.

findings.title: No LocalBusiness/Organization/ContactPoint JSON-LD for AI answer engines to key off
findings.description: This is exactly the structured-data type AI Overviews and local/AI answer surfaces key off for 'is there an office here' queries, and it's entirely absent.
findings.recommendation: Add once real NAP data exists (see Schema category's TravelAgency/Organization templates).

findings.title: llms.txt is missing
findings.description: No llms.txt route exists in the codebase or as a static file. Not required by any major AI platform today, but low-effort and directly on-brief for GEO.
findings.recommendation: Add an llms.txt route mirroring the existing robots.txt.ts/sitemap.xml.ts pattern (same STAGING gate) once real content exists.

categories.name: Search Experience (SXO)
what_works: Title tags and H1s correctly match search intent for the '[Airline] [City] office' query pattern
The 'Call Now' card is well-placed above the fold — the right structural instinct, matching the click-to-call convention every competitor uses
Sidebar related-page module renders correctly on both desktop and mobile — a working component, just fed the wrong link today

findings.title: Critical page-type mismatch vs. what Google actually rewards for this query family
findings.description: Real SERP analysis of '[Airline] [City] office' queries shows Google's top-10 results (and its AI-synthesized answer, which pulled address/hours directly from this exact competitor corpus, not from official airline sources) are dominated by a Local Page x Service Page x FAQ hybrid template — 9 of 10 results reviewed fit this pattern. The target page implements only the shell: 0 of 5 required Local Page elements (NAP, geo, hours, map, LocalBusiness schema) are structurally present, independent of the placeholder-copy issue.
findings.recommendation: Add an 'Office Details' component (address, hours, map slot) backed by LocalBusiness/TravelAgency schema — the single biggest structural gap, scored as the lowest-rated element for every user persona tested.

findings.title: Call Now link uses href="#" instead of tel:, even structurally
findings.description: The one interactive element on the page points to a dead anchor rather than a tel: protocol link — this should be fixed independent of whether the phone number itself is real yet, so the click-to-call mechanism is testable pre-launch.
findings.recommendation: Change to a tel: link now, even with placeholder digits.

findings.title: No FAQ section / no FAQPage schema on the representative page
findings.description: The strongest-ranking competitor template (flyoffices.com) uses an FAQ section targeting Google's PAA-style question synthesis for this query type; the target page has none (except the fabricated one on a different page, tracked separately under Content/Schema).
findings.recommendation: Add a real FAQ component with FAQPage schema once genuine Q&A content exists.

findings.title: All 5 tested user personas score in the 'Critical Mismatch' band
findings.description: In-Person Visitor (10/100) and HQ/Corporate Seeker (13/100) score lowest — both are blocked by missing address/hours/map fields that don't exist in the template at all, not just unfilled copy.
findings.recommendation: Prioritize the Office Details component fix above all other SXO items — it resolves the two weakest personas simultaneously.

categories.name: Backlinks
what_works: Domain was registered brand-new on 2026-08-14 via NameCheap — confirmed via WHOIS, ruling out any inherited spammy link history from a prior owner

findings.title: Backlink Health Score: Insufficient data (Tier 0 only — no Moz/Bing/DataForSEO credentials configured)
findings.description: Common Crawl shows the domain not yet present in its web graph, consistent with a pre-launch, robots-blocked site. This is expected and not a launch blocker.
findings.recommendation: Configure a free Moz API key ahead of launch for an immediate post-launch baseline; re-run this check once robots.txt is opened and the site is submitted for indexing.

phases.name: Phase 1: Pre-Launch Blockers (must fix before STAGING=false)
items: Replace Lorem Ipsum body content with real, verified office data (address, phone, hours) on all 6 published location pages — the single most important gate
Remove or complete the fabricated FAQPage schema ('question 1'/'answer 1') on the Algiers page
Delete the WordPress 'Home' page or add 'home' to RESERVED_SLUGS to kill the /home duplicate-homepage bug
Delete the default 'Hello world!' WordPress post and remove it from the homepage's 'Latest Blog Posts' section; scrub the personal Gmail byline and CMS-origin sameAs disclosure
Fix the JSON-LD image domain bug so ImageObject/thumbnailUrl resolve to cms.airlineslocations.com instead of a 404ing frontend path
Replace the placeholder phone number(s) sitewide and change 'Call Now' links from href="#" to real tel: links
Upload real, location-specific images for all 6 location pages (5 currently show a broken placeholder icon)
Only after all of the above: flip STAGING=false and rebuild; verify robots.txt, noindex meta, and Sitemap: line all flip together

phases.name: Phase 2: High-Impact Structural & Technical Fixes
phases.timeframe: Week 1-2 post-launch (or pre-launch if timeline allows)
items: 301-normalize trailing-slash and case-variant URLs to one canonical lowercase form
Add LocalBusiness/TravelAgency schema per office page and Organization schema per airline hub page, gated on real NAP data
Add an 'Office Details' component (address, hours, map slot) to the location-page template — the single biggest SXO structural gap
De-duplicate the two conflicting BreadcrumbList schema blocks emitted on every content page
Fix http:// og:image/twitter:image URLs to https://
Fix double-encoded HTML entities in meta descriptions
Set a real Cache-Control on the prerendered homepage so Hostinger's edge CDN can cache it
Test Google PSI against a public build; if it 403s the same way Lighthouse did in this audit, get Hostinger to allowlist Google's fetchers at the hcdn WAF layer

phases.name: Phase 3: Content & Authority Depth
items: Add a real FAQ section with FAQPage schema, matching the strongest competitor template pattern
Add a Head Office / HQ pointer block on location pages for misrouted searchers
Replace the irrelevant 'related pages' link pattern with a real nearby/related-offices module
Add meta descriptions to all location pages once real content exists
Establish a required-fields publish gate in the CMS (no page publishable without real phone/address/hours) before scaling page volume beyond the current 6
Add llms.txt mirroring the existing robots.txt.ts/sitemap.xml.ts pattern

phases.name: Phase 4: Monitoring & Iteration
items: Re-run this audit's Backlinks category post-launch once the site is crawlable and indexed
Configure a free Moz API key for ongoing backlink monitoring
Re-run full Core Web Vitals lab measurement once the hcdn/headless-Chrome 403 is resolved
Add <lastmod> to the sitemap sourced from WP's modified field
Add /airlines and /blog to the sitemap generator's static-route list
Re-audit every future location page against this checklist before publish, given the confirmed systemic (template-level) nature of the placeholder-content issue
